content.text: Section 22 fully addresses the rule; section 23 contains only a heading with no substantive assurance obligations.

input.quote: 22.1 Vendor may audit Customer's compliance with licence quantities no more than once in any twelve-month period, on at least thirty days' prior written notice, during normal business hours, and in a manner that does not unreasonably disrupt Customer. An audit will be conducted off-site where practicable by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality.
input.rationale: Section 22 meets the preferred position in every material respect: audits are limited to once in any twelve-month period (§22.1), require at least thirty days' prior written notice, are confined to normal business hours, must be off-site where practicable and conducted by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality. Section 22.2 places audit costs on Vendor unless the audit establishes an underpayment exceeding five percent, and expressly bars Vendor and its auditor from directly accessing Customer systems, unrelated Customer Data, privileged material or another supplier's confidential information — so the walk-away concerns (unlimited/unannounced audits, remote system access) do not arise. Section 22.3 adds customer-favourable protections (findings are Customer Confidential Information, use limited to enforcement, copy of the final report, and finality on payment of a shortfall). Section 23 ("Records and Customer Assurance") contains no substantive paragraphs and adds no further audit or assurance obligations on us. No redline needed.
